rules.rule_en: Simile: In simile two unlike things are explicitly compared. A simile is introduced by words such as like, so, as etc.
Metaphor: It is an informal or implied simile in which words like, as, so are omitted.
Personification is an attribution of personal nature, intelligence or character to inanimate objects or abstract notions.
Alliteration is the repetition of the same letter or syllable at the beginning of two or more words.
Onomatopoeia is the formation of a word whose sound is made to suggest or echo the sense.
Metonymy is meant for a change of name. It is a substitute of the thing names for the thing meant.
Apostrophe is a direct address to some inanimate thing or some abstract idea as if it were living person or some absent person as if it were present.
Hyperbole is a statement made emphatic by overstatement.
Synecdoche is the understanding of one thing by means of another. Here, a part is used to designate the whole or the whole to designate a part.
In transferred epithets, the qualifying objective is transferred from a person to a thing as in phrases.
Euphemism: Using agreeable and favourable terms for an unpleasant or disagreeable person, object, or event.
Irony: The real meaning of words is different from the intended meaning. Types include Situational, Verbal, and Dramatic.
Pun: A play on the various meanings of a word; the effect is often ludicrous.
Epigram: A brief pointed saying that couples words which apparently contradict each other.
Antithesis: An opposition or contrast of ideas. Two opposite ideas are put together to achieve a contrasting effect.
Oxymoron: It is a figure of speech which combines two seemingly contradictory or incongruous words for sharp emphasis or effect.
Litotes: It is the opposite of hyperbole. Here an affirmative is conveyed by negation of the opposite.
Interrogation: A rhetorical mode of affirming or denying something more strongly than could be done in ordinary language.
Exclamation: Used for strong expression of feelings.
Climax: An arrangement of a series of ideas in the order of increasing importance.
Anti-climax: The opposite to climax; signifies a ludicrous/ridiculous descent from the higher to the lower.
Circumlocution: Consists of expressing some fact or idea in a roundabout way, instead of stating it at once.
Tautology: Meant for repeating the same fact or idea in different words.
Paradox: Contrary to expectations, existing belief, or perceived opinion. It is a statement that appears to be self-contradictory.
Understatement: A figure of speech in which a writer or a speaker deliberately makes a situation seem less important or serious than it is.
Assonance: Identity or similarity in sound between internal vowels in neighbouring words.
Consonance: The repetition of consonant sounds, usually at the end of words.
Repetition: The repetition of words or phrases to form rhythm or to emphasize an idea.
Allusion: An allusion is a figure of speech where a writer makes an indirect reference to something external to the text, such as a historical event, a literary work, a person, or a myth.
Anaphora is the repetition of a certain word or phrase at the beginning of successive lines of writing or speech.
Ellipsis is a series of dots that indicate an intentional omission of words or series of words.
A Figure of Speech is a word or a phrase which gives a different meaning from the usual one. It is used figuratively, to give an implied meaning to the given context.
Alliteration is the repetition of the same consonant letters or similar sounds at the beginning words in a set or series of words.
Imagery is the way that a writer helps reader visualize or see in their minds what is being described.
Personification is a figure of speech in which a thing, an idea or an animal is given a human attribute.
A Simile is a figure of speech, in which two unlike things are compared, using the words, 'like' or 'as'.
A Metaphor is an implied meaning; unlike Similes which compare two things with the use of words 'like' or 'as', Metaphors directly state the comparison between two things that are in no way similar.
Consonance: Repetition of similar consonant sounds in the neighbouring words.
Assonance: Repetition of similar vowel sounds in the neighbouring words.
Anaphora: Repetition of a word or a phrase at the beginning of a sequence of sentences, paragraphs and lines.
Alliteration: Repetition of consonant sounds at the beginning of words.
Epithet is an adjective or phrase expressing a quality or attribute regarded as characteristic of the person or the thing mentioned.
Imagery is the name given to the elements in a poem that sparks the senses (sight, hearing, touch, taste, smell).
Metaphor is a figure of speech that makes an implicit, implied, or hidden comparison between two things that are unrelated, but which share some common characteristics.
Metaphor: A direct comparison between two unlike things without using 'like' or 'as'.
Alliteration: The occurrence of the same letter or sound at the beginning of adjacent or closely connected words.
Personification is a figure of speech in which a thing – an idea or an animal – is given human attributes.
Assonance is the repetition of two or more vowel sounds.
Alliteration is the repetition of two or more consonant sounds.
Connotation suggests beyond what it expresses.
